title: Account for linked async requests and provisional rate-limit crediting
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: We have observed classes of customer usage where a single logical operation is executed via a chain of asynchronous API calls: a short initial request that primes the model or obtains an ID, followed by one or more follow-up requests (appends, tool calls, or resumed streams) that are causally linked. In many of these flows we currently allocate provisional rate-limit credits and tentative billing entries at the first hop, then reconcile when the chain finalizes.

Problem: Edge cases lead to double-counting or orphan provisional credits: retries of the initial hop, speculative replays, mid-chain model switches, and proxying layers that replay requests for latency reasons. Rate-limiter state and the metering ledger are not consistently coupled for provisional entries. As a result: (1) customers sometimes see transient overcharges, (2) internal dashboards show inflated concurrent usage causing aggressive throttling, and (3) rollbacks/finalizations are occasionally missed in the presence of interleaved partial responses.

Goals: Provide a robust protocol for provisional crediting of linked async requests that ensures: deterministic final token counts and single-charge semantics, idempotent reconciliation (commit/rollback), minimal impact to tail latency, and observability for debugging and audits.

Scope: server-side ledger + rate-limiter changes, lightweight session affinity metadata in proxy paths, e2e test harness for chained async flows, telemetry and dashboard updates. This ticket focuses on the core accounting semantics and implementation of a provisional-credit lifecycle; follow-ups will cover UX and billing dispute automation.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by metering and rate-limiter owners describing provisional-credit lifecycle (provisional->commit->rollback)
Server ledger accepts provisional entries tagged with provenance id and can atomically commit or rollback without leaving double-counted balances
Rate-limiter can reserve (soft) tokens for provisional entries and release them deterministically on rollback or convert to hard consumption on commit
Idempotency keys and a minimal session-provenance header are sufficient to dedupe retries across proxies
End-to-end test harness simulates chained async patterns (initial prime + 0..N follow-ups) and asserts final billing equals single-charge ground truth
Telemetry emitted for provisional lifecycle events (created, converted, rolled_back) and dashboard panels that surface orphan provisional entries older than threshold
steps_to_reproduce: Use a client that sends an initial prime request then immediately retries the prime while the follow-up arrives; observe provisional entries in the ledger for both primes
Simulate a mid-chain model switch (prime hashed to model A, follow-up hits model B) and reproduce a case where provisional was never committed
Proxy replay: configure the edge proxy to replay initial hop on 5xx to measure duplicate provisional creation
notes: We intentionally keep provisional entries separate from finalized consumption to allow fast-path acceptance without waiting for full chain completion.

Design choices to evaluate: (A) strong lease-on-provisional with automatic expiry and background reconcile vs (B) lightweight provisional with guaranteed explicit commit from the finalizer. Both have tradeoffs on recovery complexity.

This ticket does not change pricing model or UI-facing invoices; it's focused on internal ledger invariants and rate-limit correctness. Billing UI changes will be a follow-up once ledger semantics are stable.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial report from support: Customer ACME reported 2 transient charges for a single document-synthesis flow. Gathered traces and a tentative reproduction. Assigning to metering core.

2026-02-18 - Liam O'Connor: Spike concluded. Root cause: proxy retry + provisional write during prime. See spike notes in attached design doc. Proposal: add provenance-id header and provisional anchor with commit token.
2026-02-25 - Priya Menon (SRE): We need TTL on provisional entries to avoid indefinite orphaning—recommend 24h expiry and background reconcile job. Added as acceptance criteria.

2026-03-03 - Design review: Agreed on provisional->commit->rollback semantics. Chosen approach: lightweight provisional with explicit commit. Edge-case plan: background reconcilers for expired provisionals and audit hooks for manual correction.
2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Implementation PR opened for ledger API changes (see attachments). Running integration tests against the e2e harness. Marking status In Progress.
